title: Resolution comparison for the hypercohomology edge
statement: Let $F:A\to B$ and $G:B\to C$ be additive left exact functors between Grothendieck abelian categories with derived categories [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and assume F sends injectives to G-acyclics [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. Let $X\in A$, $I$ an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and $n\geq0$. The composite $H^n(GF(I))\to R^n(F\circ G)(X)\to G(R^nF(X))\to G(H^n(F(I)))$, formed from the inverse resolution comparison, the canonical Grothendieck left edge [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps], and G of the F-resolution comparison [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], equals $\ell_G(F(I),n)$ [def-pc-hypercohomology-left-edge]. This is a map on all homology, and contains no supplied cycle lift or quotient equation.

source.place: Tags 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor) and 015N (lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence); representative calculation expanded from lem-pc-grothendieck-cocycle-comparison

proof.text: Expand the canonical Grothendieck target isomorphism at p=0, q=n. Generalize the integer homology index m before substituting m=0+n so the dependent casts disappear by equality elimination. The remaining truncation and shift factors are exactly hypercohomologyLeftEdgeTargetIso. Naturality of rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf moves the ordinary homology comparison past the degree-zero derived functor. These steps are proved by the two private helpers in the item module.

Obtain the resolution isomorphism e and its ordinary-homology and composite-unit equations from the resolution unit comparison, for the prescribed I. Extend F(I) by zero as L; its quotient is cohomologically nonnegative.

Apply Abelian.SpectralObject.leftEdge_naturality to hypercohomologySpectralObjectFunctor.map e.hom. Apply naturality of hypercohomologyLeftEdgeTargetIso to e.hom. Compose the latter equation with G of the quotient/extension homology comparison and use the ordinary resolution equation to identify the target factors.

Expand grothendieckLeftEdgeMap into source comparison, truncation edge, and target comparison. Substitute the target equation, then left-edge naturality. At the bottom/top truncation the spectral-object map is H^n(RG(e)); substitute the composite-unit equation. Associate compositions: the result is exactly the definition of cochainHypercohomologyLeftEdge.
